evidence.notes: Active voice, which French prefers; the batch related_examples give exactly this active/passive pair (Les croisés envahissent le pays. / Le pays est envahi par les croisés.). Confidence high.

entity_key.title: Adjectives change meaning based on position

patches.value: un grand homme (= un homme illustre)

evidence.notes: Placing grand before the noun gives the meaning 'great/illustrious'; after the noun (un homme grand) it means 'tall'. The context lists grand among the adjectives whose meaning changes with position. Uncertainty low.

patches.value: Ce professeur est apprécié de ses étudiants.

evidence.notes: Taken from the batch related_examples; de is used after verbs of emotion or opinion, where the agent plays a less active role, whereas par marks a truly active agent. Confidence high.

entity_key.title: Color adjectives from nouns are invariable

evidence.notes: Marron is a noun-derived color adjective (the chestnut), so it stays in the masculine singular form and takes no plural -s. Context explicitly names marron. Confidence high.
Compound color adjectives such as vert clair remain in the masculine singular form; neither element agrees. Context names vert clair and gris foncé. Confidence high.

entity_key.title: Compound demonstrative pronouns may be derogatory

evidence.notes: Acceptable neutral use of a compound demonstrative pronoun about a person who is present; the trap is the condescending use of celui-ci/celui-là about an absent person. This is a pragmatic/register contrast rather than a grammatical error, so the paired incorrect form is the derogatory usage. Uncertainty moderate.

Devoir plus infinitive expresses probability here ('he must be ill'); the same construction can express obligation, disambiguated by intonation. Context confirms the obligation/probability ambiguity of devoir. Confidence moderate-high.

entity_key.title: Distinguishing imparfait and passé composé usage

evidence.notes: A bounded completed event on a specific occasion takes the passé composé, as the context states; the imparfait would be used for description, habit, or an interrupted ongoing action. Confidence high.
Meilleur is the irregular comparative of bon and agrees with the subject; the context names meilleur, mieux and pire as the irregular forms. Confidence high.
Généreux has the irregular feminine généreuse (-eux to -euse), one of the examples named in the batch description. Confidence high.
